messages.subject: Long run time using pardiso
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm running a model with 6200 observations and 1428 mesh nodes. I'm using these options:

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(pardiso.license= "~/pardiso.lic")
inla.setOption(mkl=TRUE)
inla.setOption("num.threads", 8)

And this is my formula and model code:

formula <- resp ~ 0 + intercept + f(i, model=spde_RE1, group=i.group, control.group=list(model="ar1")) + f(time, model = 'rw2') + f(cluster, model="iid", param=c(0.5, 5e-4)) + f(survey, model='iid', param=c(0.5, 5e-4)) + f(time.unstruct, model = 'iid', param = c(0.5, 5e-4)) 

res <- inla (formula, data=inla.stack.data(stack), family="zeroinflatedpoisson1", offset=log(pig_data@data$mem.pigs), control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), link=1), control.inla=list(strategy='adaptive', int.strategy='eb'),
               control.compute=list(config = TRUE), num.threads=inla.getOption("num.threads"), verbose=TRUE)

There are 17 time knots, 6200 clusters, and 13 surveys. This model is taking 17 hours to run on a Linux server. Do you have any ideas on how I can speed this up? The output from verbose==TRUE is below

Thanks,
Julianne
